content:Speaker user says: Is there a way to set up a separate feed or sidebar on Twitter that displays recommended content based on my interests and the people I follow, without having to sift through retweets and duplicate content?: March 2016 – Things I think.
I just went through my entire list of people I was following on Twitter and cleaned house. Even though my following count was only just over 100, I’ve begun to really dislike scrolling through my feed without having gained any useful knowledge. Did I really need to spend those few minutes looking at my feed? Did I gain anything of value besides finding a way to spend a few minutes (minimum) of my life?
In deciding who to unfollow, there were so many people that I thought were interesting but didn’t necessarily publish content on a day to day basis that I was interested in. There’s so much duplication of content that I need to sift through when scrolling through my feed. I love baseball and so I follow a lot of baseball related accounts, but that doesn’t necessarily mean that I want to see a majority of baseball content in my feed- it just means I want to see a variety of baseball content/sources in my feed. I ended up creating a baseball list devoted to baseball accounts that I followed. Now if I want to hear some baseball stuff, I’ll have to search the dark corners of Twitter to get to said baseball list; Seriously Twitter, why even have a Lists feature if it’s so hard to access?
The same is true for politics: I might follow a few Bernie Sanders related accounts but I don’t want to be bombarded with a Bernie tweet ever 15 minutes. I might just be following them because I think he’s an interesting guy and want some Bernie related content. Some people publish rich original content occasionally that I don’t want to miss out on, but I don’t want to have the added cost of having to sift through the remainder of what they publish.
A separate feed or sidebar that contains content either retweeted by people I follow, or recommended content based on who I follow and what I like. It’s interesting that some accounts with the most interesting content often retweet other interesting content, which I may also appreciate. The problem comes when 2 or 3 people are retweeting the same interesting content. Recognize when there’s duplication- only show me once. context:The speaker expresses frustration with excessive content duplication and lack of value in their Twitter feed, proposing a customized sidebar or separate feed as a solution to display curated content based on specific interests and followed users. They mention utilizing tools like TweetDeck and Nuzzel to filter out duplicate content and provide a more tailored experience. keywords: Twitter, Lists, feed, interests, duplication, retweets, sidebar, content, filtering, knowledge tags: content_curation, feed_management, information_filtering, list_organization, third_party_tools, customization_solutions, twitter_alternatives

content:Speaker user says: Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: How has Freshwork been able to expand its product offerings quickly?

Passage: Cloud-based customer engagement platform Freshdesk Inc has rebranded itself as Freshworks Inc, the company said in a statement.
The rebranding exercise is part of the San Bruno- and Chennai-headquartered company’s efforts to position itself as a multi-product brand and to provide more product clarity. Until now, Freshdesk was not only the name of the company but also its eponymous flagship product offering.
“We felt that the company brand (Freshdesk) was not doing justice to the other products. It was limiting our ability to tell our multi-product story to the world,” said Girish Mathrubootham, chief executive of Freshworks.
According to Mathrubootham, the company had been toying with the idea since April last year. It decided to go ahead with rebranding itself around three months ago after Freshsales, its fourth product offering, was launched last year and crossed the 1,000-plus customer mark.
“While it might be considered a risky move, particularly when the brand is established, we also did not want to give away the multi-product strategy until we really had enough products,” he added.
The company’s flagship product Freshdesk was launched in 2010 and allows organisations to support customers through multiple channels like email, phone, websites, mobile apps, forums and social media. The company has since gone on to launch Freshservice, a cloud-based service desk and IT service management solution to address IT support needs; Freshsales, a full-featured customer resource management solution for sales teams handling high-velocity leads; and Freshcaller, a fully functional call centre on the cloud. According to the company’s website, a fifth offering called Glowboard, a platform for social reviews of products, is also in at the trial stage.
Freshwork’s products are currently used by more than 100,000 customers across 145 countries. According to Mathrubootham, more new product announcements are in the offing by the end of this year.
“We are completely focused on business software. Every product we introduce will invariably help teams inside companies to engage and collaborate better, thus translating into a better consumer engagement experience,” he said.
Freshworks has also made seven acquisitions till date, which has given it a quicker runway to launch other products. They include SaaS-based data integration platform Pipemonk, social chat platform Chatimity Software Pvt. Ltd, Faridabad-based Memeticlabs Technologies Pvt. Ltd, Pune-based visual collaboration platform Framebench, in-app customer support platform Konotor, social recommendations platform Frilp, and video chat software 1Click.io.
Founded in 2011 by former Zoho employees Mathrubootham and Shan Krishnasamy, Freshworks is backed by the likes of Capital G (formerly Google Capital), Tiger Global, Sequoia Capital and Accel Partners, and has raised close to $150 million in external funding till date, according to data available with VCCEdge, the data research platform of News Corp VCCircle.
The company has global offices in India, the UK, Australia, and Germany, and counts Honda, Bridgestone, Hugo Boss, University of Pennsylvania, Toshiba and Cisco among its customers.
Recently, Freshdesk also launched its own app marketplace for developers and clients. It competes with the likes of homegrown Zoho and US-based global player Salesforce. context:The speaker inquires about the specific reasons behind Freshwork's recent company rebranding and the strategic necessity driving the decision. keywords: Freshworks, rebranding, multi-product strategy, acquisitions, customer engagement tags: corporate_identity_shift, strategic_motivation, brand_evolution, freshwork_rebranding, multi_product_strategy, ceo_leadership, acquisition_details, product_launch_timeline, venture_capital_funding, global_operations, analytics_reporting, customer_engagement_tools, product_clarity

content:Speaker assistant says: Definitely! Here are some tips for taking accurate measurements and choosing the right fabric for your sewing projects:

1. Taking accurate measurements: When measuring yourself or someone else for a sewing project, make sure to use a tape measure and measure at the widest point of each area (chest, waist, hips, etc.). Make sure the tape measure is level and not too tight or loose. Take multiple measurements to ensure accuracy. 2. Choosing the right fabric: When choosing fabric for a sewing project, consider the weight and drape of the fabric. For example, a lightweight cotton fabric may be suitable for a summer dress, while a heavier fabric like denim may be more appropriate for a jacket or pants. Also, make sure to check the care instructions on the fabric to ensure it is suitable for your project. 3. Test fabrics: If you're not sure which fabric to use for your project, try purchasing a small piece to test out first. This way, you can see how the fabric handles, how it drapes, and how it feels against your skin. 4. Use a fabric guide: If you're still unsure about which fabric to choose, consult a fabric guide or a sales associate at a fabric store. They can advise you on which fabrics will work best for your project. I hope these tips help! Remember, practice makes perfect! Don't be afraid to make mistakes and learn as you go. context:This content provides essential guidance on how to take accurate body measurements and select appropriate fabrics for sewing projects by considering weight, drap, and testing materials. keywords: sewing, fabric, measurements, tips, projects tags: fabric_selection, measurement_techniques

content:Speaker user says: The most notable thing to me about Gala 2017, our fourth, was its feeling of intimacy. The coming together of old friends, the arrival of new ones, in a new venue (as the evening unfolded, the wraparound windows of Tribeca 360 revealed the lights of lower Manhattan), all contributed to the warmth of the event.
Most memorable of all was this year’s chair, Walter Bernstein. His remarks about the power of words, used well or badly (they can as easily convey lies as truths, and must therefore be respected and chosen with care), gave special power to the entire evening’s celebration.
Walter lived through a period when artists were pressured to conform to political pressures alien to their nature or risk losing their livelihood. His integrity and courage through this time are an inspiring reminder of how to resist mounting pressure from the growing misuse and abuse of language in our public discourse.
Sharon Robino-West, a participant in our workshops, who has both served in the military and as a caregiver to a family member, spoke movingly about her work with the WGI and how writing has helped her articulate and gain a sense of control over her life experiences.
This year we worked with a new population: exonerated prisoners who served sentences for crimes they didn’t commit. Jessica Blank, who spearheaded this outreach, spoke to us about this new initiative and was joined by Natheson Fields, who served twenty years on death row before he was found to be innocent of the crime that had put him behind bars. Their report of the workshop’s impact on exonerated prisoners has encouraged us to expand our work with this population.
The heart of the evening, as always, was a presentation of pieces written in our workshops, all on the theme of “Change.” It amazes me to hear this work read aloud. Our guests comment over and over that it’s hard to believe some of our participants have never written before. As I listened to these experiences recounted – a confrontation with a schoolyard bully, an experience in combat, an encounter with an old boy friend – I was amazed at how these emerging writers found the words to make their experiences come so vividly alive.
The variety and vitality of the work was extraordinary and the presentation by our actor/friends, William Jackson Harper, Emily Skeggs, Tony Shaloub, Eisa Davis, Brook Adams and Mandy Patinkin was riveting from start to finish.
Year after year, our producers Richard Dresser and Willie Reale, along with director Jonathan Bernstein, find a way to weave this work into a tapestry of voices that brings entire worlds to life, worlds we might never have the privilege to otherwise encounter. You’ll find some of this work on our website. And more will be written in the year (and years) ahead.

content:Speaker assistant says: Software testing compatibility with hardware is crucial to ensure proper functioning of the software on the particular hardware platform. It is essential because:

2. Avoids software crashes: Compatibility issues between software and hardware can result in system crashes, data loss, and other severe issues. Thorough testing of compatibility can prevent these problems, which can lead to improved user experience, trust, and customer loyalty.

3. Cost-effective: Compatibility testing at an early stage can save a lot of time and money by detecting compatibility issues before it reaches the end-user. Resolving issues post-deployment can be time-consuming, expensive, and can adversely affect the user's trust in the software.

4. Improves market share: Compatibility testing ensures that the software functions properly on a wide range of hardware platforms, and this results in an increased user base, leading to more revenue and better market share.

content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, let me explain.

How compatibility testing can affect the software's performance:

1. Hardware Configuration: Compatibility testing ensures that the software behaves in the same way across a range of hardware types and configurations. If the software is not compatible with some particular hardware, it may result in poor performance, latency, or crashes.

2. Operating System Versions: Compatibility testing for different operating systems is necessary as different operating systems have different APIs that can impact the software behavior. A change in the operating system version can cause compatibility issues like different graphics drivers, disk drivers, and other dependencies that may impact the software's performance.

3. Web Browser Compatibility: Websites and web-based applications must undergo compatibility testing for various browsers to ensure cross-browser compatibility. Web applications function and look differently on different browsers, and compatibility testing helps identify any issues and fix them.

Factors to be considered during compatibility testing:

1. Supported Hardware: The software compatibility testing should be performed on a range of hardware types, including different configurations, from different manufacturers.

2. Operating System: Compatibility testing should be carried out on various operating systems that support the software.

3. Third-party applications: It is crucial to check the compatibility of the software with other related applications that run on the same system.

4. Database Compatibility: Compatibility testing should be performed with different databases that are required for the software.

5. Documentation: It is essential to document all the test cases and results to ensure that compatibility testing has been carried out rigorously.

In conclusion, compatibility testing is vital to delivering high-quality software that performs well across various hardware and software configurations. It ensures that the software works seamlessly on the intended platform, minimizing risks, and improving user experience. context:This content reviews Microsoft's Windows 3.0 and related software tools, the IBM PS/1 home computer, and programming language improvements, highlighting their features, market impact, and suitability for home and professional computing environments. keywords: Compatibility testing, performance, hardware, operating systems, cross-browser compatibility tags: compatibility_testing_framework, performance_optimization, testing_methodology, platform_verification, cross_browser_testing, database_compatibility, documentation_standards, operating_environment_evolution, home_computing_strategy, multitasking_enhancement, productivity_software, microsoft_ecosystem, early_personal_computer_history

content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, here are some examples of compatibility issues that can arise between software and hardware during testing:

1. Driver Compatibility: One of the most common compatibility issues is the inability of the software to recognize drivers installed on a computer system. Sometimes, software may not have the correct drivers that are required to run on a particular hardware platform.

2. Memory Compatibility: Different hardware have different memory configurations. Compatibility issues can arise when software is unable to allocate and manage its memory on a specific system, resulting in poor performance and crashes.

3. Processor Compatibility: Some software may not run optimally on specific processors, which can lead to software crashes, system hangs, and other performance-related issues.

4. Peripheral Compatibility: Compatibility issues can arise with peripherals like printers, scanners, or cameras. The software may not recognize or function correctly with the specific hardware, leading to unexpected behavior or system crashes.

5. Operating System Compatibility: Software must be compatible with different operating systems as each OS varies in its architecture, functionality, and feature set. Incompatibility with the operating system can result in installation errors, conflicts with other installed software, or system crashes.

In conclusion, compatibility issues can arise due to various hardware configurations and software requirements. content:Speaker assistant says: Certainly, here are some methods used to perform compatibility testing:

1. Manual Testing: Manual testing involves having a tester use the software on different hardware platforms, operating systems, and browsers to verify compatibility. It involves running a set of test cases and using the software in a real-world scenario. This method is time-consuming, but it helps to find issues that automated tools might miss. 2. Automated Testing: Automated testing involves using specialized tools to test software on different hardware, browsers, and operating system configurations. The tests are automated, which means they can efficiently execute large test suites quickly, and can also help to identify bugs and other issues faster. 3. Virtualization: Virtualization tools allow developers to create virtual machines that mimic different hardware configurations, operating systems, and browser environments. Developers can use virtual environments to test the application on various configurations, minimizing the need for physical devices. 4. Cloud-Based Testing: Cloud-based testing is a newer approach to testing that utilizes cloud computing. Software applications are deployed on a cloud system that simulates different configurations, enabling the software to be tested using real-world scenarios. 5. Beta Testing: Beta testing involves releasing the software to a group of beta testers who use the software in real-world scenarios on different hardware and software configurations. This method provides the software team with feedback regarding the software's compatibility with various configurations. content:Speaker assistant says: The internet has its roots in a 1960s U.S. Defense Department project called ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network). It was designed to help researchers share information across long distances using packet-switching technology. In the 1970s, ARPANET was extended to European research institutes, establishing the first international network. In 1983, ARPANET switched from a network using the NCP protocol to a new protocol suite called TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol), which has continued to be the basis for the internet.

In the 1980s, access to the internet was mostly limited to universities and government agencies, but in 1991, a computer scientist named Tim Berners-Lee introduced the World Wide Web (WWW) as a way to search for and access information on the internet using hypertext links. This innovation quickly made the internet accessible to everyone.

Since then, the internet has transformed almost every aspect of our personal and professional lives, including how we communicate. With email, instant messaging, chat rooms, social media, and video conferencing, people can now communicate with others all over the world instantaneously and almost for free. The internet has also transformed the business world, enabling e-commerce, online banking, and telecommuting. content:Speaker assistant says: Sure, here's a step-by-step guide on how to create a GPO using the Group Policy Management Console (GPMC) in Windows Server:

1. Log in to your Windows Server and launch the Group Policy Management Console (GPMC). You can do this by going to Start > Administrative Tools > Group Policy Management.

2. Once you have opened the GPMC, you will see a list of domains and organizational units (OU) in the left pane. Select the domain or OU where you want to apply the GPO.

3. Right-click on the domain or OU name and select "Create a GPO in this domain, and link it here..."

4. In the "New GPO" dialog box, enter a name for the new GPO and click "OK".

5. You will now see the new GPO listed in the GPMC console. Right-click on the GPO and select "Edit".

6. The GPO editor will open. Here, you can configure various settings for the GPO, such as user and computer settings, security settings, software installation, etc. For example, if you want to restrict access to the control panel, you can navigate to User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Control Panel and enable the "Prohibit access to the Control Panel" setting.

7. After you have made the desired changes to the GPO, close the GPO editor.

8. You can now link the GPO to the desired OU by right-clicking on the OU and selecting "Link an Existing GPO". Select the GPO you just created and click "OK".

9. To apply the GPO immediately, you can run the "gpupdate" command on the target client computers. Alternatively, you can wait for the next scheduled refresh of Group Policy (usually every 90 minutes).

That's it! You have now created a GPO using the Group Policy Management Console in Windows Server. Note that there are many more settings and options available in the GPMC, so feel free to explore the tool further to see what else you can do with GPOs. context:Speaker assistant introduces the Pomodoro Technique as a popular time management method for improving productivity and focus. keywords: Group Policy Object, Group Policy Management Console, Windows Server, Administrative Templates, gpupdate tags: pomodoro_introduction, time_management_methods, productivity_techniques, focus_strategies, step_by_step_technique

content:Speaker user says: A Lewis Martin header, which cancelled out an early goal from Dean Shiels, saw a second-string Pars side draw with the runaway division winners Rangers. In an effort to rest his mainstays for the forthcoming play-offs, Jim Jefferies had changed his entire starting eleven, but has now given himself some selection headaches as his understudies performed superbly.
I remember a pre-season friendly against Wigan Athletic (I think) where the manager made eleven substitutions at half-time. However, I can’t recall a serious match where the manager has rested his entire starting eleven from the previous week, but that is what happened here, as the Pars started with Goodfellow in goals, a back 5 of Williamson, Young, Potter, Martin and Whittle, a midfield trio of Byrne, Spence and Graham, and a striking partnership of Dargo and Smith. On the bench there was a little bit more experience, where Page, Husband and Millen retained their squad places, but we also saw some new faces in goalkeeper Jamie Wilson, forward James Thomas who has scored a double for the young Pars at Newtongrange, and fringe first teamers O’Kane and Mercer.
Rangers, with an under-20s league decider coming up, named, in contrast, pretty much their best available team: Bell in goals; a back four of Faure, Mohsni. McCulloch and Smith; Peralta, Law, Black and Aird in midfield, and Daly and Shiels up front.
Given the number of hidings the Pars have had off Ibrox sides in the past, there were some reservations about this match-up; the fact it was a meaningless end of the season match did little to quell the concerns.
After a brief interruption allowing ground staff to apply sand to a flare that was thrown on the pitch by the visiting support, Lee McCulloch won the toss, and decided to play "the wrong way" by defending the Norrie McCathie end in the first half. If this was a ruse to put the Pars off, it certainly worked initially, as the Pars took a few minutes to settle. Spence conceded an early free-kick and soon after Byrne the first corner on his left-hand side. Aird took this and drove in a low ball that McCulloch turned on target but Goodfellow saved well low to his left.
It took the Pars a few minutes to get into the opposition half, but Dargo sprung the offside trap, but didn’t have the sharpness to get away from Faure who tackled to give the Pars their first corner, but Whittle’s delivery was deep and caused no issue. The Pars had a second half chance when a free-kick was knocked into the box, but although Allan Smith did well to get the ball onto his right foot, he didn’t connect properly with his follow-up.
Rangers were looking to get the ball forward to Shiels and Daly, but the quality of pass was wanting, and all Goodfellow had to do was decide from which side to take the subsequent bye-kick. There was more danger in 14 minutes, when a Spence foul conceded a free-kick 25 yards from goal in a central position. Steven Smith had already scored from a similar position against the Pars at Ibrox, but this time the wall was well positioned, and although Mohsni got his head to the subsequent corner, he couldn’t find the target.
Rangers were now enjoying the bulk of possession, with Law and Black coming deep for the ball, but for all that they weren’t creating much – the Pars were getting men behind the ball, and making things difficult for their more experienced opponents. A cross from Aird looked dangerous, but Martin headed skywards, and Goodfellow plucked the ball from the air, before another deep cross found its way to Black at the edge of the box but Goodfellow saved comfortably.
The Pars enjoyed a decent spell as well – Graham did well to keep his nerve under pressure from Aird as the visitors sought to break, and although he was rather harshly booked not long after, he continued to look for the ball, and after he found Willamson on the overlap, Cammy Bell had to be alert to grab the cross almost off the toe of Allan Smith.
Another Aird cross caused difficulties – Martin headed away from under his own crossbar – and when the corner came in McCulloch nodded back for Mohsni to head off the bar. However, that was the closest Rangers came to scoring and although the visitors were ahead on points, the game was scoreless.
The Pars needed to keep equality for 10 or so minutes in the second half if they were to ramp up pressure on the visitors but managed to concede a goal within 30 seconds of the restart. Rangers came forward, a slip by Young allowed Law to turn on to his right to fire in a shot and although Goodfellow blocked that one he could do nothing about the follow- up as Shiels netted from close range. content:Speaker user says: Can you give a brief summary of Pedro Caixinha's first game as Rangers manager?: Gers cruise past Accies to get their new manager off to a perfect start.
Pedro Caixinha's Rangers reign got off to a flying start, with a resounding win over Hamilton at Ibrox.
First half goals from Emerson Hyndman and Clint Hill had the Gers cruising at half-time, before second half strikes from Martyn Waghorn and Lee Wallace.
Caixinha made one change to Graeme Murty's team which drew at Celtic Park, Jon Toral returning from injury to replace Lee Hodson, with James Tavernier moving to right-back.
Perhaps mindful of the 6-0 beating his side suffered on their last visit to Govan, Accies manager Martin Canning named a starting XI without a recognised striker.
Emerson Hyndman created the first opportunity of the game after Kenny Miller had played a delightful ball out wide to him, but his low cross evaded everyone in the box.
Four minutes later, another fine ball to the wing from Miller saw Barrie McKay cut inside and lay the ball on for Jason Holt, but he sent his effort over the bar.

content:Speaker user says: A Lewis Martin header, which cancelled out an early goal from Dean Shiels, saw a second-string Pars side draw with the runaway division winners Rangers. In an effort to rest his mainstays for the forthcoming play-offs, Jim Jefferies had changed his entire starting eleven, but has now given himself some selection headaches as his understudies performed superbly.
I remember a pre-season friendly against Wigan Athletic (I think) where the manager made eleven substitutions at half-time. However, I can’t recall a serious match where the manager has rested his entire starting eleven from the previous week, but that is what happened here, as the Pars started with Goodfellow in goals, a back 5 of Williamson, Young, Potter, Martin and Whittle, a midfield trio of Byrne, Spence and Graham, and a striking partnership of Dargo and Smith. On the bench there was a little bit more experience, where Page, Husband and Millen retained their squad places, but we also saw some new faces in goalkeeper Jamie Wilson, forward James Thomas who has scored a double for the young Pars at Newtongrange, and fringe first teamers O’Kane and Mercer.
Rangers, with an under-20s league decider coming up, named, in contrast, pretty much their best available team: Bell in goals; a back four of Faure, Mohsni. McCulloch and Smith; Peralta, Law, Black and Aird in midfield, and Daly and Shiels up front.
Given the number of hidings the Pars have had off Ibrox sides in the past, there were some reservations about this match-up; the fact it was a meaningless end of the season match did little to quell the concerns.
After a brief interruption allowing ground staff to apply sand to a flare that was thrown on the pitch by the visiting support, Lee McCulloch won the toss, and decided to play "the wrong way" by defending the Norrie McCathie end in the first half. If this was a ruse to put the Pars off, it certainly worked initially, as the Pars took a few minutes to settle. Spence conceded an early free-kick and soon after Byrne the first corner on his left-hand side. Aird took this and drove in a low ball that McCulloch turned on target but Goodfellow saved well low to his left.
It took the Pars a few minutes to get into the opposition half, but Dargo sprung the offside trap, but didn’t have the sharpness to get away from Faure who tackled to give the Pars their first corner, but Whittle’s delivery was deep and caused no issue. The Pars had a second half chance when a free-kick was knocked into the box, but although Allan Smith did well to get the ball onto his right foot, he didn’t connect properly with his follow-up.
Rangers were looking to get the ball forward to Shiels and Daly, but the quality of pass was wanting, and all Goodfellow had to do was decide from which side to take the subsequent bye-kick. There was more danger in 14 minutes, when a Spence foul conceded a free-kick 25 yards from goal in a central position. Steven Smith had already scored from a similar position against the Pars at Ibrox, but this time the wall was well positioned, and although Mohsni got his head to the subsequent corner, he couldn’t find the target.
Rangers were now enjoying the bulk of possession, with Law and Black coming deep for the ball, but for all that they weren’t creating much – the Pars were getting men behind the ball, and making things difficult for their more experienced opponents. A cross from Aird looked dangerous, but Martin headed skywards, and Goodfellow plucked the ball from the air, before another deep cross found its way to Black at the edge of the box but Goodfellow saved comfortably.
The Pars enjoyed a decent spell as well – Graham did well to keep his nerve under pressure from Aird as the visitors sought to break, and although he was rather harshly booked not long after, he continued to look for the ball, and after he found Willamson on the overlap, Cammy Bell had to be alert to grab the cross almost off the toe of Allan Smith.
Another Aird cross caused difficulties – Martin headed away from under his own crossbar – and when the corner came in McCulloch nodded back for Mohsni to head off the bar. However, that was the closest Rangers came to scoring and although the visitors were ahead on points, the game was scoreless.
The Pars needed to keep equality for 10 or so minutes in the second half if they were to ramp up pressure on the visitors but managed to concede a goal within 30 seconds of the restart. Rangers came forward, a slip by Young allowed Law to turn on to his right to fire in a shot and although Goodfellow blocked that one he could do nothing about the follow- up as Shiels netted from close range.
